explanations.text:
●  what the skill is                            ([decompile-claude](decompile-claude))
│     Claude does two things: it abstracts a file, and it maps the
│     abstraction. The map lives in one record next to the file, and
│     a folder of files has one record of its own. Only the tool
│     writes them. Each map run adds one abstraction and changes
│     none before it.
│
●  how you point at things             ([how you point](How the user points at things))
│     You paste words, not numbers. Claude finds which abstraction
│     the words belong to.
│
●  pins                                                    ([anchors](1. Anchors))
│     A pin ties a few words to a piece of the file, to the words of
│     an earlier abstraction, or to another file of the folder. The
│     rules: pin the name, keep the words unique, point at real
│     things, make no circle. The rest of the text is free.
│
●  how claude abstracts                                    ([explain](2. Explain))
│     Who the reader is: someone who knows the subject, not the code.
│     The first abstraction covers the whole file. The rules of plain
│     words: define a word before it is used, say for what a thing
│     exists, keep the verbs. Show the abstraction, then stop.
│
●  how claude maps                                             ([map](3. Map))
│     On your word, the text goes to the tool as it is. The tool
│     checks the pins and adds one abstraction. A detailed one is
│     mapped before the simpler one that points into it.
│
●  reword and take back                     ([rewrite](4. Rewrite and rollback))
│     New words for one abstraction, in place, keeping the pins that
│     others depend on. Undo removes the last one.
│
●  when the file changes                      ([sync](5. Sync after a change))
│     Once per change. The tool carries the pins to the new lines;
│     claude mends only the words that went untrue.
│
●  what claude reports                                       ([report](6. Report))
      The new abstraction, the coverage, the warnings, and the offer
      of the next one.
